turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): I am sorry we are late, Doctor. The robot at the bottom of Main Road was out and the traffic was quite bad.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ag, don't stress. Umm, give me a moment, this computer is taking forever to open your file.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We did leave at half past eight. She's been quiet the whole drive, poor thing.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that again? The screen just blinked. Who have you brought with you?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): This is my mother, Doctor. Mrs Naidoo. I asked her to come with me, if that is acceptable.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Of course it is. Right. So, what can I do for you today?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): I would like to discuss contraception, please. I am twenty two, and I am hoping for something more reliable than condoms.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. Have you used the pill before?

[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor. I was taking Nordette for contraception, one tablet by mouth every day, for six months. I beg your pardon, I miscounted, it was nine months, and then I stopped.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): And why did you stop? Hang on, this thing has frozen again. Why did you stop?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): Because of headaches, Doctor. They came most afternoons, quite bad, just behind my eyes.
[SEG0012] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She was missing lectures over them. I had to fetch her from campus twice.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, can you repeat the timing for me? Err, when did the headaches actually start?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): About two months after I started the Nordette. Once I stopped, they settled within a week.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any flashing lights with them, or weakness down one side?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. No flashing lights, and no weakness. It was only the headache.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your periods, are they regular?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor. They come every month. They are not particularly heavy either.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke at all?
[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Not really every day. Sometimes at a party, not really.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Eish, the screen jumped. Is that a yes or a no? I need it for the method.
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): I would not call myself a smoker, Doctor. Perhaps a cigarette in a month, if that.
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ag, even that worries me. Her father smoked his whole life and we all lived with it.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ja, noted, sort of. Let me take your pressure while this loads. One twenty eight over seventy six, no, sorry, one eighteen over seventy six.
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Is that acceptable, Doctor?

[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ja, that's a normal reading. I think those headaches were probably from the oestrogen in the combined pill, seeing as they came on after you started and went once you stopped. I would not put you back on a combined pill.
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): I understand. What would you suggest instead, please?

[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): There's the mini-pill, taken every day, the injection, Depo-Provara, every 12 weeks, a copper device, or the implant in the arm. The implant lasts three years. Sorry, did you get that last bit?
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor, three years. Um, the implant sounds the most sensible to me, though I would prefer to read about it before I decide.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We'll go through it at home. I had a clot in my leg when I was on the pill, at thirty two. They said it was the oestrogen.

[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Shame, thank you, that's important. A clot in your mother is another reason for me to stay away from oestrogen. I'll give you the implant leaflet now. Have a proper read, and don't start any tablets before we meet again.
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): Thank you, Doctor. When ought I to return?
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Book 2 weeks from today. If you have decided on the implant by then, we can arrange to put it in. Reception will give you the time on the way out.
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): Thank you very much. We will read the leaflet carefully and I will come back in two weeks with my decision.

spec.situation: Young woman asks about contraception, previous pill caused headaches, smokes occasionally; blood pressure read; options discussed; implant leaflet given, decision next visit.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats
